Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
8:54 AM

People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying faster, cheaper and easier than cash or cards, and it works on almost any smartphone.

Before UPI, paying a small shop or a friend meant carrying change, finding a cash machine or waiting for a card swipe. Now you scan a code or type a mobile number, enter your PIN, and the money moves from your bank account in seconds. Even a tea stall or a vegetable seller can accept it with a printed QR code.

The three big reasons:

Free and instant. Most everyday payments cost the user nothing, and the money arrives at once, at any hour, even on holidays.
Works across banks. You can pay anyone, whichever bank or app they use, without any long setup.
Easy for small sellers. They need no card machine or contract, just a QR code, so more shops take it every year.

Trust helps too. Every payment needs your PIN, and banks, apps and the government all pushed it until it felt normal. Once most of your local shops accept UPI, carrying cash starts to feel like the odd choice.
